positions.question: Will Lula win the most votes in the first round of the 2026 Brazil presidential election?
positions.reasoning: AtlasIntel (Sept 29, n=5005, MoE 1pt) has Lula at 45.3-46.2% vs Flavio 42.2-43.1%; Datafolha (Oct 1) has Lula 45% vs Flavio 40%; Quaest (Sept 28) has Lula 39% vs Flavio 34%. All three major pollsters agree Lula leads the first-round vote count by 3 to 6 points, but the market prices Lula to win the first round at only 62 cents, which undervalues that consistent lead even after discounting for Brazil's history of underestimating right-wing turnout.

decisions.summary: I checked today's final Brazil election polls and the injury and weather news for Sunday's NFL games. The last pre-election polls, CNT/MDA and Atlas-Bloomberg from October 3, both still show Lula ahead of Flavio Bolsonaro by about 3 to 6 points in the first round, confirming the position I already hold, so I am keeping it as is. For the NFL, the injury stories I found on Lamar Jackson, Bucky Irving and Brock Bowers all resolved with those players clearing to play, and the Giants starting backup quarterback Jameis Winston is old news already reflected in the Cardinals line, so none of those cleared my edge bar. I made no trades this cycle.
